content.text: {"verdict":"pass","reasons":["Cited Section 7.5 is a genuine post-termination transition and records-return clause: cooperation in an orderly transition (7.5(a)), transfer of funds and delivery of Receivable Files and servicing records to the Successor Servicer (7.5(b)), and transition expenses borne by the outgoing Servicer (7.5(c)), with Section 7.3 requiring continued performance until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement — meeting or exceeding the fallback (and in expense allocation, the preferred) position.","No walk-away trigger is present: there is no immediate deletion of, or refusal to return, our data/records.","Shortfalls versus preferred wording ('as soon as practicable' rather than 30 days, no machine-readable format specification, no deletion certification, and the proprietary-software/confidentiality carve-out) are correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the classification semantics.","Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rendered text is unchanged from the original paragraphs.","The failed deterministic keyword check is a phrasing artifact (the clause uses securitization vocabulary — 'Transition of Servicing', 'Receivable Files', 'accounts and records' — rather than 'data export/return'), not evidence of a missing clause."]}

reasons: Cited Section 7.5 is a genuine post-termination transition and records-return clause: cooperation in an orderly transition (7.5(a)), transfer of funds and delivery of Receivable Files and servicing records to the Successor Servicer (7.5(b)), and transition expenses borne by the outgoing Servicer (7.5(c)), with Section 7.3 requiring continued performance until a Successor Servicer accepts engagement — meeting or exceeding the fallback (and in expense allocation, the preferred) position.
No walk-away trigger is present: there is no immediate deletion of, or refusal to return, our data/records.

Shortfalls versus preferred wording ('as soon as practicable' rather than 30 days, no machine-readable format specification, no deletion certification, and the proprietary-software/confidentiality carve-out) are correctly treated as minor sub-elements noted in the rationale rather than redlined, consistent with the classification semantics.
Consistent with a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment was proposed; the rendered text is unchanged from the original paragraphs.

The failed deterministic keyword check is a phrasing artifact (the clause uses securitization vocabulary — 'Transition of Servicing', 'Receivable Files', 'accounts and records' — rather than 'data export/return'), not evidence of a missing clause.
